# dsh-memory-curator

Curated durable memory for DeepSeek Harness: automatic
capture of decisions, corrections, prohibitio

ns and open work; progressive-disclosure recall;
duplicate consolidation; and old-vs-new conflict re

solution. Everything is local — one JSON
store under `$DSH_HOME`, no network of its own, no account,

no API key. Model calls reuse the
Harness `llm` service, so memory inherits the user's provider, cr
edentials and retry policy.

## What it does
| | Behaviour | How |
| **A. Auto-capture** | When a turn ends, the conversation is distilled into durable entries worth k
eeping across sessions: designated technical references, architecture decisions, explicit correction
s, prohibitions, and unfinished work. | A fire-and-forget listener on `session/event` (`turn/end`) s
ends the new messages to one bounded auxiliary LLM call; the validated candidates are persisted. Mem

ory work can never delay or fail a turn. |
| **B. Progressive recall** | Each turn gets a bounded on
e-line-per-entry index: the entries that change behaviour (decisions, corrections, prohibitions, ope
n work) come first, then the most recent facts. Full text is fetched only on demand. | A resident ca
talog is injected into the system prompt (tier 0). `memory_search` returns short digests with ids (t
ier 1). `memory_detail` returns the complete entry (tier 2) and records the read, which feeds the or

dering and the decay pass. The standing prompt cost stays flat as the store grows. |
| **C. Curation
** | Duplicate knowledge folds into one entry; a newer decision on the same subject retires the outd
ated one. | A deterministic pass runs on every insert and periodically: same-subject decisional entr
ies conflict, the newer wins, the older is kept as history with a `supersededBy` pointer. A model-as
sisted pass adjudicates the similar-subject pairs the deterministic pass cannot settle, biased towar
d `coexist` so a true memory is never wrongly retired. |
## What memory does not record

The plugin deliberately does not overlap with the artifacts a project already keeps. Any one
of thes
e tests means *record nothing*:
| Test | Where that information belongs instead |
| Would a future session get it from the repository? Architecture, file paths, build and test comman

ds, dependency lists, directory layout, git history. | The code and git themselves. |
| Is it a proj
ect-level instruction — a convention, an "always/never" rule? | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, where eve
ry teammate and every tool sees it. Memory is machine-local and invisible to the rest of the team. |
| Is it task state — progress, next steps, a worked-off plan? | `STATE.md`, a todo list, or the iss

ue tracker. |
| Is it a report that something was just done? "published the repository", "rewrote th
e history", "added a section". | The artifact is its own record. |

To make the first two decidable rather than a matter of taste, every distillation call carries
the r

epository context: the bounded text of `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` when they exist, plus the
names of

`README.md`, `STATE.md`, `TODO.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/`

. Reads are cached by mtime and size, so a quiet repository costs a
few `stat` calls per turn.

What is left is the part with no other home: environment and tooling traps, the user's own
preferenc
es and corrections, and facts about this machine that the repository cannot know.

Credentials are the one case where a prompt is not enough. `lib/store.js` redacts
credential-shaped

strings (`sk-…`, `ghp_…` / `github_pat_…`, `AKIA…`, `xox…`, JWTs, PEM private
keys) at the single wr

ite choke point every path goes through, so an auto-capture, a tool call
and a panel paste are all c

overed. Redaction beats rejection: the sentence around a leaked key
is usually the part worth keepin

g, so the entry survives with `[redacted]` where the secret was.
The patterns name credential shapes

, not "anything that looks random" — a commit id or a sha256
digest is untouched.

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

No build step. The host half declares `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` as peer d

ependencies (provided by the Harness runtime);
the browser half needs only `react` (supplied by the
client module loader).

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is a **development-only** dependency for
`npm test`: the schema contract te

sts compare this plugin's compiler and schemas
against the Harness's real `parameterSchemaSpecToJson

Schema` /
`assertSupportedJsonSchema`. They skip themselves when it is absent, so the
plugin still r
uns and tests from a bare checkout with no dev install.

Inside a sandboxed DSH shell, plain `npm test` fails with `spawn EPERM`: Node's
test runner starts o

ne child process per test file and captures its output over a
pipe, which the sandbox does not allow

. `npm run test:in-process` runs the same
suite in a single process instead.
### 运行完整功能所需的最低权限
**`仅可查看`（Read Only）即可运行全部功能。**
四种会话权限模式（仅可查看 / 工作区内修改 / 完全权限 / Auto review）约束的是**智能体的内置工具**，而非插件宿主代码：
- 文件工具（`read`/`write`/`edit`）经 `dsh-fs-sandbox`（沙箱化的 `ctx.fs` 提供方）围栏，其 README 明确写道：它限制的是"**模型对**文件的写

入与编辑"，围栏"是在可信代码中检查**模型控制路径**的策略，而非内核边界"——即在文件工具层内检查，并非全局 `fs` 拦截。
- Shell 工具（`bash`/`pwsh`）以子进程方式由 `

dsh-bash-sandbox`/`dsh-pwsh-sandbox` 隔离；插件代码运行在宿主进程，不在受限子进程内。
- `Auto review` 审查原生工具调用，不围栏插件宿主代码。
